Merge sort is a divide-and-conquer algorithm that works by recursively splitting an array into smaller subarrays until each subarray contains only one element. These single-element subarrays are inherently sorted. The algorithm then merges these subarrays back together in a sorted manner. The merging process involves comparing the elements from the two subarrays and placing them in the correct order in a new array. This process continues until the entire array is merged and sorted.

Merge sort is preferred over quicksort for linked lists because it has a guaranteed O(n log n) time complexity in all cases, whereas quicksort can degrade to O(n²) in the worst-case scenario. Additionally, merge sort is more efficient for linked lists because it can merge two sorted linked lists in O(n) time without requiring additional space for copying elements, which is necessary for arrays. This makes merge sort a better choice for sorting linked lists.
